# 04 Two measured gaps: a dotted arrow's short spelling, and `linkStyle`'s `color`

## Outcome

Two things this board itself discovered are settled by measurement rather than left as prose: the
dotted arrow spelling Mermaid draws and Siren refuses, and the one author declaration that now has
an element it could paint.

## Why this ticket exists

Both were found *by* tickets in this board, both were correctly left alone at the time, and both are
behavior changes — which is why they are not in the closing ticket, whose write ownership is
`examples/`, `demos/`, `CONTEXT.md` and the records. A closing ticket that changed the parser would
blur the commit boundary this board has kept for three tickets.

## Part A — `A .-> B`

**Measured by ticket 02** (mermaid 11.17.2): `A .-> B` is `type="arrow_point" stroke="dotted"
length=1`, and `A .- B` is the `arrow_open` of the same. Siren refuses both, because the dotted body
pattern is `-\.+-`, which requires a dash on *both* sides of the dots. The same gap is why
`A -. yes .-> B` cannot close an inline label here while `A -. yes -.-> B` can.

Corpus row `fc-edge-dotted-short` already exists, `rejected`. It is the row ticket 02 wrote rather
than fix, on the grounds that an arrow *spelling* belongs to the ticket that decomposed the arrow
token. That ticket has landed; this is where it gets paid.

- [ ] **Measure the whole family before changing the pattern**, with `pnpm --filter @siren/core
      probe`, not from the two spellings named above: `.->`, `.-`, `..->`, `...->`, `-.->`, `-..->`,
      `.-->`, `<.->`, `.-o`, `.-x`, and the inline-label forms `A -. yes .-> B` and
      `A .- yes .-> B`. Report the table. Some of these will be parse errors in Mermaid; a spelling
      Mermaid refuses is one Siren must refuse too, and knowing which is the point of the table.
- [ ] Every spelling Mermaid draws, Siren draws, with the same line, ends and length.
- [ ] **Carried warning, and it is the exact shape of a regression ticket 01 caused and caught.**
      When ticket 01 made the arrow separator a pattern rather than a literal, `style A
      --my-token:4` started being cut as a malformed edge. It found this by asking *what else could
      contain `--`*, not by waiting for a test. Ask the same question about `.`: a declaration value
      (`stroke-width:1.5px`, `stroke-dasharray:5.5`), a quoted label containing `.->`, a node label
      `A[".-> literally"]`. Say what you checked.
- [ ] `fc-edge-dotted-short` moves to `supported` with a semantic assertion — the line style read
      off the drawn edge, not "it parsed".

## Part B — `linkStyle 0 color:#f00` and the edge label

**This is a measurement, not a taste decision, and the ticket turns on what you measure.** Board 3
routes an author's `color` into a style's *text* half; ticket 02 gave an edge a text element for the
first time and deliberately did not connect the two, because doing so changes what an existing
directive does. What happens today is pinned by `index.test.ts :: leaves \`linkStyle\`'s \`color\`
off the label` — the declaration is resolved, reaches `renderToSVG`, and is dropped silently.

The judgement is simple once measured: **if Mermaid paints an edge label with `linkStyle`'s `color`,
then Siren dropping it is a silent mis-render**, which this project's absolute condition does not
permit. If Mermaid ignores it too, Siren ignoring it *is* the compatible behavior and the pin stays.

- [ ] **The existing probe cannot answer this and must be extended.** Verified before writing this
      ticket: `mermaid-probe.mjs` prints the parser db — vertices, edges, subgraphs, direction — and
      `linkStyle 0 color:#ff0000,stroke:#00ff00` does not appear anywhere in its output. Answering
      needs the rendered SVG and the computed paint on the label's `<text>`. Extend the probe so
      that this class of question is answerable *again* later, and document the new mode in its
      header comment the way the existing modes are. This is the same reasoning that made the probe
      committed code rather than a scratch script.
- [ ] Report what you measured, for `color`, and for `stroke` beside it so the two can be compared.
- [ ] **Act on the measurement, and say which branch you took.** If Mermaid paints the label:
      translate and wire it — ADR-0008 already settled that `color` becomes `fill` on SVG text and
      that translation exists for node text; reuse it rather than minting a second path. Replace the
      pin with a test of the new behavior and say in the report that you replaced it. If Mermaid
      does not paint it: leave the wiring alone, keep the pin, and record the agreement as a corpus
      row so the next reader finds a measurement rather than a silence.

## Corpus

Measured at `3747ec3`: **58 supported / 15 rejected / 3 silently-wrong**. Expect `REJECTED` 15 →
**14** from Part A; Part B adds a row of some kind whichever way it goes. `SILENTLY_WRONG` stays 3 —
none of its rows is this board's, and it has not moved in three tickets.

These are an **expectation, not a quota**. Both tickets before you raised `rejected` by writing down
a gap they measured rather than staying inside a number I gave them, and both were right to. If the
family table in Part A turns up a spelling Mermaid draws that is too large to land here, write the
row and say so.
